q: At the opening of stores tenders, a representative of a tenderer who is present asks the officer opening the tenders to negotiate the rates then and there, offering to reduce his firm's rate on the spot. The correct course is that:

options.A: The negotiation is held at the opening itself and the reduced rate is recorded as the firm's offer
options.B: All the tenderers present are asked to reduce their rates turn by turn at the opening
options.C: No negotiation is conducted at the stage of opening of tenders; the offers as submitted are evaluated by the Tender Committee, and any negotiation thereafter is held only in accordance with the rules
options.D: The tender of the representative's firm is rejected for making the request

q: The acceptance of a stores tender is communicated to the tenderer by a letter of acceptance issued within the validity period of his offer, but the formal purchase order is issued a few days later. The tenderer then claims that no contract exists, as he has not received the purchase order. The correct position is that:

options.A: The tenderer is right, a contract arising only on physical receipt of the purchase order
options.B: A contract is concluded by the acceptance of the offer communicated within its validity, and the tenderer is bound to supply on the terms accepted, the purchase order following in due course
options.C: The contract arises only when the material is delivered at the depot
options.D: The tenderer may withdraw his offer freely until the purchase order reaches him

q: A contractor to whom railway stores were issued for use on a work returns the stores remaining unused with him on completion of the work. On receipt back in the depot, the returned stores are correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Examining the stores, taking the serviceable stores into stock with due credit to the work, and segregating the unserviceable stores for survey and disposal
options.B: Refusing to take back any stores once issued to a contractor
options.C: Taking the entire quantity into stock as new stores at the original issue rate, without any examination
options.D: Selling the returned stores to the contractor himself in an e-auction

q: Stores rejected on inspection continue to lie in a depot well beyond the period stipulated for their removal by the supplier. The charges leviable on the supplier for keeping the rejected material in the depot beyond that period are in the nature of:

options.A: Demurrage for detention of wagons beyond the free time
options.B: Liquidated damages for delayed supply of fresh stores
options.C: Earnest money for participating in the next tender
options.D: Ground or storage charges for the occupation of depot space by the rejected material, as provided in the conditions of contract

q: The same stores item is issued by two depots of one zonal railway at two different issue rates, each depot applying the rate of its own last purchase. This practice is incorrect because:

options.A: The issue rate of an item is uniform at all depots of a railway, being the book rate of the item for that railway
options.B: Each depot is free to fix its own issue rate for every item
options.C: The issue rate must be fixed by the consuming department drawing the item
options.D: The issue rate must change with every fresh purchase made by a depot

q: Stores declared surplus in a depot are required by a department of the Central Government, which offers to take them over before they are put to auction. Subject to the sanction of the competent authority, the stores may be disposed of by:

options.A: Free gift to the Government department, surplus stores being of no use to the Railway
options.B: Sale to that department at the book value plus the prescribed departmental charges, sale to other Government departments being a recognised mode of disposal of surplus stores
options.C: Sale only after the department participates and succeeds in the e-auction
options.D: Transfer to the department without any entry in the stores accounts

q: A narrative report of a stock verifier brings out a procedural irregularity in a depot, the stock sheet for quantities stands closed, but the same irregularity is found repeated at the next verification of the depot. The correct handling of the matter is that:

options.A: The irregularity is ignored, the stock sheet having already been closed
options.B: The stock verifier prepares a fresh stock sheet for a shortage of the same value
options.C: The irregularity is condoned by the stockholder himself by a note in the bin card
options.D: The matter is pursued by the Accounts office with the stores authorities for compliance and remedial action, and is brought to the notice of the competent authority so that the irregularity does not recur

q: The stock of an item in a depot has just touched its minimum level, and the quantity ordered against the re-order level is still in transit. The position is correctly understood as that:

options.A: Procurement action for the item is to be initiated for the first time at this stage
options.B: The minimum level is the buffer meant to meet demands while the replenishment already initiated at the re-order level is in transit, and the dues in transit are to be progressed for early receipt
options.C: The item is to be declared surplus, its stock having fallen to the minimum
options.D: All issues of the item are to be stopped until the next annual review

q: Tools and plant held by a field department are produced for the periodical verification of such articles by the department. A few articles borne on the Tools and Plant register are not produced and are reported missing. Until the loss is regularised, the missing articles:

options.A: Stand automatically struck off the register on the date of the verification
options.B: Are replaced free of cost by the stores depot without any enquiry
options.C: Continue to be shown as outstanding in the register against the official responsible for their custody, pending recovery of their cost or write-off under competent sanction after enquiry
options.D: Are treated as stores consumed on the work without any record

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Internal check of stores bills in the Accounts office, exercised before the bills are passed for payment, is a check carried out within the Railway's own accounting organisation.
2. Audit of the stores accounts by the Railway Audit organisation is the statutory external audit conducted on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Vetting of an indent by Finance is exercised at the demand stage, before procurement is taken up, and examines the availability of funds and the propriety and justification of the demand.
2. The Tender Committee functions after the tenders are opened, and evaluates the offers received and recommends the offer to be accepted.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Under a stores contract containing a price variation clause, a supplier claims a price increase worked out on an index of his own choice which is not referred to in the contract. The claim is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Accepting the supplier's index, it being the latest available
options.B: Allowing the increase at the discretion of the consignee depot
options.C: Cancelling the contract and inviting a fresh tender for the balance quantity in every such case
options.D: Working out any price adjustment only with reference to the indices and the formula stipulated in the contract itself

q: A Tender Committee, instead of accepting the lowest offer as made, makes a counter-offer to the lowest tenderer at a lower rate, which the tenderer declines. The legal position of the counter-offer is that:

options.A: The original offer stands accepted at the counter-offer rate, the tenderer having no choice
options.B: A qualified acceptance or counter-offer does not by itself conclude a contract; on its rejection by the tenderer, no contract arises on those terms and the tender is dealt with further in accordance with the rules
options.C: The tenderer is bound to supply at the counter-offer rate after a fixed period
options.D: The earnest money of the tenderer is forfeited for declining the counter-offer

q: In the two-packet system, a tenderer's techno-commercial packet is opened and is found not to contain the Earnest Money Deposit required to be furnished with that packet. The correct course is that:

options.A: The price packet of the tenderer is opened first and the deposit is collected later
options.B: The deposit is recovered from the earnest money of another tenderer in the same tender
options.C: The offer is treated as incomplete and non-responsive in accordance with the tender conditions, and its price packet is not opened
options.D: The tenderer is allowed to furnish the deposit after the tender is decided

q: In a tender, the lowest bid is of a non-local supplier. A Class-I local supplier whose bid is within the margin of purchase preference is given the opportunity to match the lowest price, but he declines to do so. The order is then correctly placed:

options.A: On the Class-I local supplier at his own quoted price, preference being absolute
options.B: On the non-local lowest bidder, the local supplier having declined to match the lowest price
options.C: By splitting the order equally between the two suppliers at their own rates
options.D: On neither, the tender being discharged in every such case

q: A supplier completes the supplies under a stores contract, but liquidated damages for delayed supply remain recoverable from him and the warranty period for the stores has not yet expired. His Security Deposit is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Refunding it in full on completion of the supplies, the dues being waived
options.B: Forfeiting the entire deposit in every case of delayed supply
options.C: Adjusting the dues recoverable from him in accordance with the contract and refunding the balance after satisfactory completion of the contract obligations, including the warranty period, as per the contract conditions
options.D: Transferring the deposit to the earnest money for his next tender automatically

q: Stores are transferred from a depot of one zonal railway to a depot of another zonal railway. The receiving railway objects to the transfer value, pointing out that it holds the same item at a lower book rate. The transfer is correctly priced at:

options.A: The lower book rate of the receiving railway
options.B: The current market rate of the item
options.C: An average of the book rates of the two railways
options.D: The book rate of the issuing railway, at which value the receiving railway takes the material into its stock through the transfer accounts

q: An item manufactured in a railway workshop is transferred to a stores depot for stocking. Its cost of manufacture, comprising material, labour and on-cost, works out higher than the price at which a similar item is available in the market. The item is nevertheless taken into depot stock at:

options.A: The market price of the similar item
options.B: A nominal value, the workshop cost being ignored
options.C: Its cost of manufacture as worked out through the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, that being the value at which workshop outturn is taken into stock
options.D: Half of its cost of manufacture, as a compromise

q: During the arrangement of stock in a depot, a quantity of material is found lying in a ward without any Price Ledger number or identifying record. Before such material can be stocked and issued in the regular course, it is necessary to:

options.A: Identify the material and allot it its proper codification, so that it is brought on record and accounted for as an identified stores item
options.B: Treat it as scrap and include it in the next e-auction at once
options.C: Issue it to the first department which demands it, identification being unnecessary
options.D: Return it to the supplier who supplied stores last to the depot

q: A railway office requires ordinary office computers of a common-use nature which are available on the Government e-Marketplace, and in the same month a railway-specific stores item, not a common-use item, is required by a depot. The two requirements are correctly procured by:

options.A: Procuring both requirements through open tenders on IREPS, GeM being inapplicable to the Railways
options.B: Procuring both requirements by local spot purchase through a committee
options.C: Procuring the common-use computers through GeM and the railway-specific stores item through tendering on IREPS
options.D: Procuring the computers through IREPS and the railway-specific item through GeM in all cases

q: While issuing stores, a storekeeper himself notices that the physical quantity in the bin does not agree with the balance shown on the bin card. The correct course for him is to:

options.A: Alter the bin card himself to match the physical quantity and continue issues
options.B: Report the difference promptly to the controlling officer so that it is verified and brought on record through the stock verification process, without altering the records on his own authority
options.C: Make good the difference from the stock of a similar item held in another bin
options.D: Wait silently until the next stock verifier happens to visit the depot

q: A receipt of stores has been posted in the Priced Stores Ledger, but to the folio of a wrong PL item, though the total quantity and value posted are correct. The error is rectified by:

options.A: Recovering the value of the receipt from the storekeeper as a shortage
options.B: Deleting the receipt note from the depot records
options.C: Transferring the quantity and value from the wrong folio to the correct folio of the item, linked with the receipt note, so that each item's priced account shows its correct balance
options.D: Altering the quantities on both the bin cards concerned without any priced adjustment

q: A supplier despatches material to a depot although no purchase order has been placed on him for it. On arrival of the unsolicited material, the depot correctly:

options.A: Does not take the material into stock and creates no payment liability, the supplier being required to take it back at his own cost
options.B: Takes the material into stock and pays for it at the supplier's billed rate
options.C: Issues the material to the first department which asks for it
options.D: Sells the material in the next e-auction and pays the proceeds to the supplier

q: A consignment despatched by a supplier for another depot is delivered at this depot by mistake. The material is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Taking it into this depot's priced stock as its own receipt
options.B: Issuing it to a consuming department of this depot
options.C: Selling it as scrap, the consignee being unknown
options.D: Holding it under intimation to the purchase office and the correct consignee, without booking it as this depot's receipt, and disposing of it as advised under proper transfer documents

q: A purchase order is placed on F.O.R. destination terms, but the supplier's bill claims freight charges separately in addition to the contract price. In internal check, the Accounts office correctly:

options.A: Passes the bill in full, freight being always payable in addition
options.B: Passes the bill at the contract price, disallowing the freight claimed separately, the F.O.R. destination price already covering delivery at the destination depot
options.C: Recovers the freight amount from the consignee depot's imprest
options.D: Debits the freight amount to the Stock Adjustment Account

q: Stores are being issued from a depot for a deposit work, and the amount deposited by the outside party for the work stands exhausted. Further issues of stores for that work are correctly made:

options.A: Freely, the cost being adjusted at the end of the work
options.B: Against the earnest money held from stores tenderers
options.C: Only after the party makes good the deposit or the debit for further issues is otherwise covered, issues for a deposit work being made at the party's cost
options.D: By charging the cost to the ordinary revenue of the Railway

q: An outside party deposits the book value of stores to be issued to it, but omits the prescribed departmental charges. The stores are correctly issued to the party:

options.A: Only after the full amount, comprising the book value plus the prescribed departmental charges, has been deposited by the party
options.B: At once, departmental charges being waived for a party which pays promptly
options.C: Against a verbal assurance that the charges will be paid later
options.D: After recovering the charges from the depot storekeeper

q: In a stores tender, negotiations are held with the lowest tenderer (L1) in accordance with the rules, but the tenderer does not agree to reduce his rate and the negotiations fail. The correct course thereafter is that:

options.A: The order is placed on L1 at his original rate in every case
options.B: The earnest money of L1 is forfeited for not reducing his rate
options.C: The depot storekeeper negotiates informally with all the other tenderers
options.D: Negotiation is not shifted to the next higher tenderer (L2) as a matter of course; the tender is dealt with further, e.g. by discharge and fresh action, as decided by the competent authority

q: Against a stores tender, a tenderer submits the sample required under the tender conditions, but the sample fails the prescribed test and does not conform to the specification. The offer is correctly treated as:

options.A: Acceptable at a reduced rate fixed by the depot storekeeper
options.B: Not acceptable for that item, the sample submitted by the tenderer having failed to conform, and the offer is dealt with as non-responsive in the evaluation
options.C: Acceptable if the tenderer promises to improve the quality after the order is placed
options.D: Referred to the stock verifier for acceptance

q: The Finance member of a Stores Tender Committee records his dissent from the rate recommended by the other members, considering it unreasonable. The correct handling of the case is that:

options.A: The dissent is deleted from the proceedings at the instance of the other members
options.B: The tender is automatically accepted at the rate favoured by the Finance member
options.C: The dissent is recorded in the Tender Committee proceedings and placed before the Tender Accepting Authority, who decides the case, recording his reasons where he differs from a recorded view
options.D: The tenderer is informed of the dissent and asked to revise his rate

q: A defect in stores is noticed and a warranty claim is lodged on the supplier within the warranty period, but the supplier actually carries out the repair only after the period has expired. The claim is correctly treated as:

options.A: Valid, the claim having been lodged within the warranty period, and the supplier remains bound to repair or replace the defective stores under the warranty clause
options.B: Time-barred, the repair not having been completed within the warranty period
options.C: Payable only if the depot pays the repair charges itself
options.D: Converted into a claim for liquidated damages for delayed supply

q: The purchaser of a scrap lot sends his authorised agent, instead of coming himself, to take delivery of the lot. Delivery is correctly allowed to the agent:

options.A: On a verbal request made by the agent at the depot gate
options.B: Against the earnest money receipt of another lot purchased by the same purchaser
options.C: Only on payment of a fresh sale value by the agent
options.D: Only against the delivery order for the lot and proper authorisation from the purchaser, a gate pass being issued for the removal of the material so delivered

q: A depot holds paints whose shelf life will expire in a few weeks and for which its regular users show no immediate demand. The correct course for the depot is to:

options.A: Retain the paints in the bins until they expire and then survey them off
options.B: Circulate the availability of the paints to other depots and user departments so that they can be utilised before their shelf life expires, instead of being allowed to become unserviceable in stock
options.C: Issue the paints to its own office for general use without any requisition
options.D: Mix the paints with fresh stock so that the expiry is not noticed

q: A field official holding imprest stores is transferred, and a successor is to take over the imprest. The imprest is correctly handed over by:

options.A: The outgoing official retaining the stores until his successor demands them
options.B: Selling the imprest stores and handing over cash to the successor
options.C: Verification and accountal of the imprest at the handover, the successor taking over the stores on hand together with the account of consumption, so that the full imprest stands accounted for
options.D: Returning the entire imprest to the supplier who originally supplied the stores

q: A department submits a requisition for stores against a work which has since been completed and closed. The issue is correctly dealt with in the accounts by:

options.A: Not debiting the value of the issue to the closed work; the requisition is returned for regularisation against a proper sanction and head of account before the issue is accounted for
options.B: Debiting the closed work in all cases, the head being reopened by the depot
options.C: Debiting the value to the Stock Adjustment Account permanently
options.D: Issuing the stores free of accountal, the work being closed

q: The custodian of a stores ward proceeds on long leave and another storekeeper is to hold the charge during his absence. The temporary handover is correctly effected by:

options.A: The custodian locking the ward and taking the keys with him on leave
options.B: The officiating storekeeper taking over on the book balances without any check or record
options.C: Handing over the cash imprest alone, the stores remaining unaccounted during the leave
options.D: Verification of the balances handed over, discrepancies, if any, being brought on record, so that the officiating custodian takes over only the balances verified and accepted by him

q: During stock verification, a verifier finds stores of different items mixed together and stacked so that the bins cannot be properly counted. Apart from the quantities verified, this condition of the depot is correctly brought out by:

options.A: Recording a shortage of all the mixed items on stock sheets
options.B: A narrative report on the irregular and unsatisfactory arrangement of stores in the depot, for remedial action such as proper stacking and segregation of stores item-wise
options.C: Debiting the value of the mixed stores to Purchase Suspense
options.D: Selling the mixed stores as one scrap lot at once

q: A firm holding a rate contract for an item repeatedly fails to supply against supply orders placed on it. Besides dealing with the individual defaults under the contract, the correct course is to:

options.A: Continue placing all supply orders on the same firm indefinitely
options.B: Recover the losses from the consignee depots which placed the demands
options.C: Arrange the supplies from an alternative source as permissible, and bring the firm's performance on record for review of its registration and future consideration in tenders
options.D: Cancel the Average Annual Consumption fixed for the item

q: Stores are drawn from a depot for the periodical overhaul (POH) of rolling stock in a workshop, but the issue note shows the value under the Primary Unit for ordinary repairs and maintenance. On check in the Stores Accounts office, the issue is correctly:

options.A: Posted as shown, the Primary Unit on the issue note being never questioned
options.B: Debited to Purchase Suspense until the overhaul is completed
options.C: Charged to the workshop's imprest cash account
options.D: Corrected and charged under the Primary Unit applicable to stores for POH of rolling stock, so that the cost is booked under the correct head of account

q: The bin card of an item in a depot is lost. The custody record of the item is correctly restored by:

options.A: Preparing a fresh bin card from the storekeeper's recollection of the transactions
options.B: Treating the entire stock of the item as a shortage of the storekeeper
options.C: Closing the priced ledger folio of the item permanently
options.D: Reconstructing the bin card from the supporting receipt and issue documents, agreed with the priced stores ledger, under the approval of the competent authority

q: A stores depot is closed and its stock is to be taken over by a nominated depot. The stock is correctly transferred by:

options.A: Distributing the stock free of cost among the user departments attached to the depot
options.B: Transferring the stock to the nominated depot under priced transfer documents, the accounts of the closing depot being closed after its balances are agreed and taken over by the receiving depot
options.C: Selling the entire stock in one e-auction in every case
options.D: Writing off the entire stock through the Stock Adjustment Account

q: A firm is banned from business dealings with the Railways while a stores contract placed on it is still under execution. The outstanding position under the contract is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Paying the firm in full for the unsupplied quantity as compensation
options.B: Recovering all dues from the depot storekeeper who received the earlier supplies
options.C: Dealing with the balance supplies, the payments due and the security held in accordance with the ban orders and the conditions of the contract, and arranging the balance requirement afresh as required
options.D: Treating the material already supplied as scrap and selling it by e-auction

q: A micro and small enterprise participating in a stores tender claims the benefits admissible to it under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs in respect of the tender documents and the earnest money. The correct position is that the enterprise is entitled to:

options.A: Issue of the tender set free of cost and exemption from payment of Earnest Money Deposit, as admissible under the policy, while remaining liable to furnish the Security Deposit if its tender is accepted
options.B: Exemption from furnishing the Security Deposit also, in addition to the tender set and earnest money benefits
options.C: No benefit of any kind in a railway stores tender
options.D: Award of the order without matching the lowest price in any circumstances

q: In a stores tender, the lowest bid is of a non-local supplier and a Class-II local supplier, whose bid is within the margin of purchase preference, claims the opportunity to match the lowest price and take the order under the Make in India preference. The correct position is that:

options.A: The Class-II supplier is given the matching opportunity in preference to every Class-I supplier
options.B: The tender is discharged and a fresh tender invited for local suppliers only
options.C: The Class-II supplier is awarded the entire order at his own quoted price
options.D: The purchase-preference matching opportunity under the Order is admissible to a Class-I local supplier; a Class-II local supplier is not entitled to that preference, though he can still secure the order if he is himself the lowest bidder

q: At a Railway Consumer Depot, the quantity of High Speed Diesel found by measurement in the tanks is less than the book balance of the depot. The difference is correctly dealt with as:

options.A: A quantity difference of stores, which is investigated, the permissible handling and transit losses being taken into account, and the shortage adjusted after approval through the prescribed stores adjustment
options.B: A price difference, to be corrected by revising the book rate of the diesel
options.C: A sale, to be credited to Sales Suspense
options.D: The personal liability of the stock verifier in all cases

q: A blank receipt note book, which is an accountable form of a stores depot, is reported missing from the depot's custody. The correct course is to:

options.A: Obtain a fresh book and make no report, the missing book being blank
options.B: Report the loss promptly to the controlling officer and the Accounts office, so that the serial numbers of the missing forms are watched and their possible misuse is prevented
options.C: Debit the value of the book to the supplier of stationery
options.D: Close the priced stores ledger of the depot for the year

q: A lot of scrap sold by weight is weighed at delivery in the presence of the purchaser, and the weight is found to be more than the quantity recorded for the lot. The excess quantity is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Delivering the excess to the purchaser free of cost along with the lot
options.B: Retaining the excess in the depot without any record
options.C: Delivering only the quantity sold, the excess being taken by the purchaser, if at all, only on payment of its value at the accepted sale rate as per the conditions of sale
options.D: Cancelling the sale of the entire lot for this reason alone

q: A workshop uses stores drawn from a depot on a manufacturing job, and scrap arises in the course of the manufacture from the material so used. The scrap arising is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Retaining it in the workshop and selling it locally for workshop expenses
options.B: Treating it as the property of the workmen engaged on the job
options.C: Mixing it with the fresh stores drawn for the next job
options.D: Returning it to the stores depot, where it is taken into account and disposed of through the prescribed survey and e-auction procedure

q: Under a stores contract with a price variation clause, the stipulated indices fall, but the supplier continues to bill at the old higher rate for supplies made after the fall. The bills are correctly passed:

options.A: At the billed rate, price variation operating only in the supplier's favour
options.B: At the rate revised downward in accordance with the indices and formula stipulated in the contract, the excess billed being disallowed and recovered
options.C: At a rate fixed by the consignee depot by negotiation with the supplier
options.D: Only after the approval of the Railway Board in each case

q: Stores issued on loan to a contractor for use on a railway work are not returned by him after the completion of the work, despite demands. The correct course is to:

options.A: Write off the stores as consumed on the work without any recovery
options.B: Recover the value of the unreturned stores from the depot storekeeper
options.C: Recover the value of the stores at the rates prescribed in the contract from the amounts payable to the contractor or his security, as per the contract conditions
options.D: Sell an equivalent quantity of depot scrap to make good the loss

q: For a stores item to be procured to an RDSO specification, a tenderer offers material of an equivalent foreign specification and asks the depot to accept the equivalence. The correct course is that:

options.A: Equivalence of the offered specification is accepted only by the competent technical authority as prescribed for such items, and not on the depot's or the tenderer's own assertion
options.B: The depot storekeeper accepts the equivalence if the rate quoted is the lowest
options.C: The offer is accepted if the tenderer gives an undertaking about quality
options.D: The item is procured without any specification in such a case

q: A supplier asks for advance payment on his stores bill before despatch of the material, without furnishing the inspection certificate and the despatch documents stipulated for such payment. The advance payment is correctly:

options.A: Made in full, the supplier being a registered firm
options.B: Made from the depot's cash imprest
options.C: Credited to Sales Suspense until the material arrives
options.D: Not made, advance payment on a stores bill being admissible only against the stipulated inspection certificate and proof of despatch, as per the contract conditions

q: The material management system is temporarily unavailable in a depot, and a consuming department presents an urgent requirement of a stock item. The issue is correctly made by:

options.A: Issuing the stores on a verbal request, no record being kept until the system is restored
options.B: Issuing the stores against a duly authorised manual requisition/issue note, the transaction being posted in the system when it is restored, so that the accountal is complete
options.C: Refusing all issues until the system is restored, whatever the urgency
options.D: Asking the department to purchase the item itself and claim reimbursement

q: A stockholder disputes the physical count of an item recorded by the stock verifier during verification. The correct course is that:

options.A: The stock sheet is destroyed and the verification abandoned
options.B: The stockholder's own count is recorded in place of the verifier's count in all cases
options.C: A joint recount of the item is carried out in the presence of the stockholder, the difference as finally ascertained is recorded on the stock sheet, and the stockholder's representation, if any, is noted for the decision of the competent authority
options.D: The difference is recovered in cash from the stockholder on the spot

q: A depot receiving stores on transfer from another depot finds, on receipt, a shortage against the quantity shown in the transfer note. The receiving depot correctly:

options.A: Takes into stock only the quantity actually received, recording the shortage on the transfer document, so that the adjustment/claim for the shortage is settled with the despatching depot
options.B: Takes into stock the full quantity shown in the transfer note, the shortage being ignored
options.C: Refuses to accept any part of the consignment
options.D: Recovers the value of the shortage from its own storekeeper

q: While vetting the Average Annual Consumption proposed for an 'A' category stock item, Headquarters Finance finds the proposed figure to be much higher than the consumption trend and the coverage it would create. The correct course on vetting is to:

options.A: Pass the figure as proposed, vetting of AAC being a formality
options.B: Refer the item to the supplier for fixing the consumption figure
options.C: Delete the item from the Priced Vocabulary
options.D: Examine the proposal with reference to the past consumption, the anticipated programmes and the stock and dues already available, and moderate the AAC to a justified figure, so that excess procurement and locking up of capital are avoided

q: Non-stock material procured against the specific demand of a work is received at a depot, but the work is cancelled and the indentor does not take the material. The material is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Returning it to the supplier in all cases at the Railway's cost
options.B: Examining it and, if serviceable, taking it into depot stock for circulation as surplus to other users, the work or demand concerned being given due credit/adjustment for the material not used by it
options.C: Issuing it to the depot staff for office use
options.D: Destroying it, a non-stock item being incapable of being stocked

q: Successive stock verifications of a depot bring out repeated shortages of 'attractive' items such as copper and brass fittings, though each individual shortage is small. The correct handling of the pattern is that:

options.A: Each shortage is ignored, the individual values being small
options.B: The fittings are issued thereafter without any requisition to save accountal
options.C: The matter is pursued as a systemic custody failure — custody and issue control over such items is tightened, surprise checks are considered, and responsibility for the shortages is investigated and fixed, instead of treating each shortage as an isolated routine difference
options.D: The book rates of the fittings are increased to cover the shortages

q: The Security Deposit of a supplier has been furnished as a bank guarantee, and the guarantee is due to expire before the warranty period of the stores supplied under the contract comes to an end. The correct course is to:

options.A: Treat the contract as closed on the expiry of the guarantee
options.B: Require the supplier to get the guarantee renewed or extended so that it remains valid for the period for which the deposit is required under the contract, recovery being effected as per the contract if he fails to do so
options.C: Recover the guarantee amount from the depot storekeeper
options.D: Refund the supplier an equivalent amount in cash from the depot imprest

q: A supplier, while acknowledging a purchase order, records exceptions to some of its conditions and proceeds on that basis. The correct position is that:

options.A: The supplier's exceptions automatically amend the purchase order
options.B: The depot storekeeper may accept the exceptions by a note on the receipt note
options.C: The exceptions have no effect unless they are formally accepted and given effect to by an amendment to the purchase order issued by the competent authority, with the concurrence of Finance where the amendment has financial implications
options.D: The purchase order stands cancelled in every such case

q: The books of account of a stores contractor are examined under the book examination clause, and the examination shows that the costs claimed by the contractor were padded. The correct action on the finding is that:

options.A: No action lies, the examination being only for information
options.B: The stock verifier revises the contract rate himself
options.C: The contractor is asked to supply all future orders free of cost
options.D: The excess claimed is disallowed and recovered, and the price payable is dealt with in accordance with the contract, under the orders of the competent authority

q: A department demands an item by a PL number which has since been deleted from the Priced Vocabulary, the item being no longer stocked. The demand is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Treating the item as a current requirement to be examined on its merits and procured, if justified, as a specific/non-stock requirement, the deleted PL number being not revived by the depot on its own
options.B: Issuing a similar item from stock against the deleted number without any record
options.C: Allotting the deleted PL number to a different item then in demand
options.D: Refusing to examine any requirement of the department thereafter

q: Stores held in the custody of a user department outside the stores depot are verified by the department, and a shortage is found. The shortage is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Automatic write-off by the department without any enquiry or sanction
options.B: Enquiry into the shortage and fixation of responsibility in the department, the loss being recovered from the person responsible or written off under the sanction of the competent authority, on the same principles as a loss of stores in a depot
options.C: Recovery of the value from the depot storekeeper who originally issued the stores
options.D: Adjustment of the value against the earnest money held from tenderers

q: Material procured as a non-stock item against a work is consigned by the supplier directly to the consignee at the work site, instead of being routed through a stores depot. On its arrival at the site, the material is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Taking it into the priced stock of the nearest depot in all cases
options.B: Inspection and acceptance by the consignee at the site, the receipt being duly accounted for and the cost charged direct to the work concerned, as for a non-stock procurement
options.C: Refusing the consignment, non-stock material being never consigned to a work site
options.D: Treating the material as the contractor's own stores at the site

q: An 'insurance spare' held in a depot for an important equipment is demanded by a department for routine, non-emergency use on other equipment. The correct course is to:

options.A: Issue the spare freely, all stock in a depot being interchangeable
options.B: Sell the spare to the department against cash payment
options.C: Reserve the spare for the breakdown contingency of the equipment for which it is held, the routine requirement being met from regular stock or procurement, unless the competent authority directs otherwise after review
options.D: Declare the spare as dead surplus, it having not been issued for a long period

q: A stores tender is received in the purchase office after the due date and time fixed for submission of tenders in the tender notice. The tender is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Opening it along with the other tenders, the delay being only marginal
options.B: Not considering it for the tender, a tender received after the due date and time being liable to be ignored and returned unopened as per the tender conditions
options.C: Accepting it on payment of a penalty by the tenderer
options.D: Treating its rates as the lowest rates for negotiation with the timely tenderers

q: A tenderer submits his offer for stores without signing the tender form and the offer, though the tender conditions require the offer to be signed by the tenderer or his authorised representative. The offer is correctly treated as:

options.A: Valid, signature being a mere formality in stores tenders
options.B: Valid after the depot storekeeper attests the copy retained in the depot
options.C: Incomplete and non-responsive, and liable to be rejected, the unsigned offer not binding the tenderer
options.D: Accepted after the purchase order is issued and signed by the Railway

q: After the tenders for a stores item have been opened, but before the tender is decided, a tenderer sends an unsolicited revised offer quoting a lower rate than his original offer and asks that the revised offer be considered. The correct course is that:

options.A: The revised offer cannot be considered, an offer being decided as submitted and opened, and entertaining a post-opening revision would vitiate the tender
options.B: The revised offer is substituted for the original offer in the comparative statement
options.C: All other tenderers are asked to revise their offers in the same manner
options.D: The tenderer is debarred for having sent the revised offer

q: The Earnest Money Deposit furnished by a tenderer whose stores tender is accepted is dealt with, on acceptance of the tender, by:

options.A: Refunding it in full in every case on the date the purchase order is issued
options.B: Crediting it to the revenue earnings of the railway
options.C: Forfeiting it, acceptance of the tender being conditional on a fresh Security Deposit in cash
options.D: Retaining it and adjusting it towards the Security Deposit to be furnished by the firm for due fulfilment of the contract, the balance, if any, being furnished separately

q: A consignment of stores despatched by a supplier against a purchase order reaches the consignee depot, but the quantity found on receipt is less than the quantity shown in the despatch documents and the inspection certificate. The depot correctly:

options.A: Takes the full quantity shown in the documents into stock, the difference being a book adjustment
options.B: Takes into stock only the quantity actually received and accepted, recording the shortage and reporting it to the purchase office and the supplier for further action
options.C: Refuses the entire consignment for the shortage of a part of it
options.D: Recovers the value of the shortage from the depot storekeeper

q: At night, a depot receives a written emergency requisition for a stock item urgently required to restore train services, the regular issue documentation not being completable at that hour. The issue is correctly made by:

options.A: Refusing the issue, stores being never issued outside office hours
options.B: Issuing the stores on a verbal request, with no record to be made at any stage
options.C: Issuing the stores against the written emergency requisition and completing and linking the regular issue note and accountal on the next working day
options.D: Selling the stores to the requisitioning department against cash payment at the depot

q: A depot holds both new stores and reconditioned (repaired and made serviceable) stores of the same description and Price Ledger number. For correct custody and issue, the reconditioned stores are:

options.A: Kept segregated and distinctly identified from the new stores, so that the two are not mixed up in stock or issued in mistake for each other
options.B: Mixed with the new stores in the same bin without any distinction
options.C: Treated as scrap, reconditioned stores being not issuable
options.D: Kept in the personal custody of the stock verifier

q: During stock verification of a depot, it comes to notice that the stockholder has brought in stores borrowed from another depot shortly before the verification to make up a shortage in his own depot. The verifier correctly:

options.A: Accepts the physical balance as correct, the stores being physically present
options.B: Verifies only the borrowed stores and closes the verification
options.C: Recovers the value of the borrowed stores from the lending depot
options.D: Disregards the borrowed stores for the depot's balance, records the shortage of the item on a stock sheet and brings out the irregular borrowing in his narrative report

q: The reliability of the physical verification of stores carried out by the Assistant Stock Verifiers is ensured in the Accounts organisation by:

options.A: The depot custodian himself checking the verifier's count after the verification
options.B: Test-check of a portion of the verifications by the Inspector of Stores Accounts or a senior Accounts officer, so that the quality of the verification work is supervised
options.C: The supplier of the stores certifying the verified balances
options.D: Dispensing with stock sheets where the test-check is carried out

q: Successive stock verifications of an item in a depot repeatedly bring out an excess of physical stock over the book balance, and not a shortage. Apart from adjusting the excess, the pattern primarily calls for:

options.A: Recovery of the value of the excess from the stockholder
options.B: Immediate sale of the excess quantity as scrap
options.C: Investigation into the receipt accounting of the depot, a recurring excess indicating receipts taken into custody without being brought on the priced accounts
options.D: Reduction of the book rate of the item to absorb the excess value

q: A purchaser of a scrap lot pays the full sale value and lifts a part of the lot within the delivery period, but does not lift the balance even after the period expires and a notice is given to him. Under the conditions of sale, the unlifted balance is liable to be:

options.A: Dealt with by re-disposal at the risk and cost of the purchaser, besides forfeiture or ground rent as provided in the sale conditions
options.B: Delivered free of charge to the purchaser whenever he chooses to lift it
options.C: Issued to consuming departments as serviceable stores
options.D: Retained in the depot indefinitely at no charge to the purchaser

q: At the time of delivery of a scrap lot sold by weight, the purchaser disputes the weighment recorded by the depot and the delivery is not yet completed. The dispute is correctly settled by:

options.A: Delivering the lot on the purchaser's own weighment in all cases
options.B: Cancelling the sale forthwith and forfeiting the entire sale value
options.C: Charging the purchaser for the higher of the two weighments without any re-check
options.D: Re-weighment of the lot before completion of delivery, in the presence of the depot representative and the purchaser, the delivery being effected on the weighment so established

q: A supplier of coal despatches a consignment booked by weight and bills for the despatched weight, but the weight found on weighment at the destination depot is less, the shortage being beyond the permissible limit for such stores. The supplier's bill is correctly passed for:

options.A: The full despatched weight billed by the supplier in all cases
options.B: The quantity actually received and accepted at the destination, the excess shortage being taken up with the supplier or carrier, as the case may be
options.C: Half of the despatched weight, as a compromise
options.D: No payment at all, the whole consignment being treated as rejected

q: A depot official who has fully used a receipt note book, which is an accountable form, applies for a fresh book. Before a fresh book is issued to him, the correct course is to:

options.A: Issue the fresh book at once, used books being of no further concern
options.B: Recover the cost of the used book from the official
options.C: Obtain back the used book and check its counterfoils and the accountal of the forms contained in it, so that no form of the book remains unaccounted for
options.D: Direct the official to destroy the used book and certify the destruction himself

q: In arranging the storage of stores in a depot, heavy items and fast-moving items in regular demand are, as a principle of economical materials handling, kept:

options.A: Near the issue and despatch section of the depot, so that handling and movement within the depot are minimised
options.B: In the remotest ward of the depot, irrespective of their movement
options.C: Mixed with inflammable stores to save storage space
options.D: In the open, without any bin or location identification

q: Steel stores which are to remain in stock for a long period are liable to deteriorate by rusting while in storage. Such deterioration in custody is guarded against by:

options.A: Issuing the stores to departments whether required or not
options.B: Reducing the book rate of the stores periodically
options.C: Recording a shortage on a stock sheet every year for the rusted quantity
options.D: Preservative treatment of the stores in storage, such as cleaning, oiling or protective coating, as a normal measure of proper custody

q: Empty drums, barrels and packing cases in which stores were received accumulate in a depot. These empties are correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Retaining them as the personal property of the storekeeper receiving the stores
options.B: Treating them as the property of the Railway, bringing them to account and disposing of them in the prescribed manner, ordinarily as scrap or by sale
options.C: Throwing them away as waste without any accountal in all cases
options.D: Returning them free of cost to whichever supplier asks for them first

q: Certain assemblies of rolling stock are maintained as a pool of repairable (rotable) stores, a serviceable assembly being issued and the failed assembly being repaired and returned to the pool. To keep the pool intact, a serviceable assembly from the pool is ordinarily issued:

options.A: Without any condition, the failed assembly being of no value
options.B: Only against cash deposit of the full price by the demanding workshop
options.C: Against return of the failed assembly of the same description by the user, so that it can be repaired and restored to the pool
options.D: Only after the failed assembly has first been sold as scrap

q: A department submits a non-stock indent for stores required for a work, but the indent does not bear the particulars of the sanctioned work or the allocation to which the cost is chargeable. Before procurement is taken up on the indent, the correct course is to:

options.A: Return the indent to the indentor for completion of the sanction and allocation particulars, procurement being not taken up on an indent which is incomplete in these respects
options.B: Procure the stores and charge the cost to Purchase Suspense permanently
options.C: Procure the stores and charge the cost to the depot's own maintenance allocation
options.D: Treat the item as a stock item and add it to the priced vocabulary

q: A supplier's bill for stores quotes a rate higher than the rate stipulated in the purchase order for the accepted quantity, though the stores themselves are accepted. In internal check, the Accounts office correctly passes the bill:

options.A: At the billed rate, the supplier's rate being the latest
options.B: At the average of the billed rate and the purchase order rate
options.C: For no payment, the bill being rejected in full for the rate difference
options.D: At the rate stipulated in the purchase order, the excess claim being disallowed and pointed out to the supplier

q: A supplier submits a second bill for a supply against which payment has already been made and the receipt note linked and paid once. The duplicate claim is prevented from being paid again in the Accounts office by:

options.A: Paying the second bill and recovering the amount from the depot storekeeper
options.B: Linking of the bill with the purchase order, the receipt note and the record of payment already made, which brings out that the supply stands paid and the duplicate bill is not passed
options.C: Referring every stores bill to the stock verifier before payment
options.D: Debiting the second payment to the Stock Adjustment Account

q: An order for a common-use item placed on the Government e-Marketplace remains unsupplied by the seller within the time stipulated in the order. The buyer correctly proceeds by:

options.A: Waiting indefinitely, an order on the portal being not cancellable in any case
options.B: Paying the seller in advance so that he supplies the item
options.C: Raising the prescribed incident and cancelling the order in accordance with the conditions of the portal, and meeting the requirement through another permissible source
options.D: Recovering the order value from the consignee depot's imprest

q: The purchases of stores of a railway during the year are regulated with reference to the Stores Budget by:

options.A: Watching the progressive outgo on stores purchases against the funds allotted for the purpose, so that purchases are kept within the allotment and additional funds are sought in time where justified
options.B: Stopping all purchases in the last month of the year in every case
options.C: Treating the Stores Budget as a mere statistical statement having no control over purchases
options.D: Charging all purchases in excess of the allotment to Sales Suspense

q: An item is stocked in a depot for the first time and has to be brought into the priced accounts of the depot. For this purpose, the Stores Accounts office:

options.A: Issues a purchase order for the item in favour of the depot
options.B: Credits the value of the item to Sales Suspense
options.C: Asks the supplier to open the account of the item
options.D: Opens a folio for the item in the Priced Stores Ledger with its Price Ledger number, nomenclature and unit of account, the stock being valued at the book rate worked out for the item

q: A purchase is made on the basis of an approved sample of the stores. The approved sample serves its purpose at the stage of acceptance of the bulk supply in that:

options.A: The sample is issued to the consuming department in place of the bulk supply
options.B: The sample is sealed and retained, and the bulk supply is compared with it on receipt to judge whether the supply conforms to the sample on the basis of which the order was placed
options.C: The sample is returned to the supplier before the bulk supply is despatched in all cases
options.D: The sample is sold as scrap along with the first lot of scrap of the depot

q: Stores returned to a depot and classified as repairable are urgently demanded by a department in their unrepaired condition, the department offering to use them as they are. The stores are correctly:

options.A: Issued at once as serviceable stores at the full book rate
options.B: Sold to the department against cash payment
options.C: Not issued as serviceable stores until they have been repaired and passed on re-inspection as fit for use, serviceability being established before issue
options.D: Surveyed off as scrap, repairable stores being never issuable thereafter

q: In a stores tender, all the acceptable offers are found to be at rates which the Tender Committee considers unreasonably high with reference to the last accepted rate and the market rate. The proper course open in such a case is to:

options.A: Discharge the tender and invite a fresh tender, instead of accepting an unreasonably high rate
options.B: Accept the lowest offer in all cases, however unreasonable the rate may be
options.C: Place the order on the highest tenderer as a penalty on the lowest tenderer
options.D: Split the order among all the tenderers at their own rates

q: A consignment of imported stores is found short-landed at the Indian port, the quantity landed being less than the quantity shipped as per the shipping documents. The Railway's claim for the short-landed stores is supported and pursued on the basis of:

options.A: The depot bin card of the consignee depot
options.B: The stock sheet prepared by the stock verifier at the consignee depot
options.C: The tender notice issued for the import
options.D: The short-landed certificate obtained from the port or shipping authorities, the claim being lodged on the shipping company or under the marine insurance cover, as applicable

q: Stores rejected on inspection are replaced by the supplier with a fresh lot. The replacement lot is correctly dealt with at the consignee depot by:

options.A: Taking it into stock without any inspection, the lot being a replacement
options.B: Subjecting it to inspection afresh and taking into stock only the quantity inspected and accepted, like any other fresh receipt
options.C: Issuing it directly to the consuming department without a receipt note
options.D: Treating it as a warranty replacement and paying a fresh price for it

q: A contractor, during the currency of the contract, fails to maintain the requisite Security Deposit, and the contract conditions so provide. The Security Deposit may in such a case be secured by:

options.A: Recovering it from the earnest money of the unsuccessful tenderers
options.B: Waiving the deposit altogether in all cases
options.C: Recovering or retaining the amount by deduction from the bills payable to the supplier under the contract, until the full deposit is made up
options.D: Debiting the amount to the Stock Adjustment Account

q: A supplier offers for pre-despatch inspection a lot of stores which is incomplete, only a part of the lot being ready and the balance still under manufacture. The inspecting authority correctly:

options.A: Declines to carry out the inspection of the incomplete lot, the material being offered again for inspection when the lot is complete and ready
options.B: Certifies the complete lot as inspected on the basis of the part offered
options.C: Issues the receipt note for the complete lot at the supplier's works
options.D: Accepts the supplier's verbal assurance for the balance under manufacture

q: A tender notice for a stores item requires supply of the full quantity tendered for, but a tenderer submits an offer for a part of the quantity only, without the tender conditions permitting part offers. The offer is correctly treated as:

options.A: An offer for the full quantity at the part-quantity rate
options.B: Automatically the lowest offer for the full quantity
options.C: A ground for cancelling the entire tender
options.D: Not in conformity with the tender conditions and liable to be treated as non-responsive for the requirement tendered for

q: A purchase order stipulates a delivery period for the supply of stores, but the supplier contends that the period should be reckoned from a later date of his own choice. The delivery period under a stores contract is reckoned:

options.A: From the date of despatch of the first consignment by the supplier
options.B: From the date of issue of the purchase order or acceptance of the tender, as stipulated in the contract, and not from a date chosen by the supplier
options.C: From the date the supplier acknowledges the purchase order, whenever that may be
options.D: From the date the material is received at the consignee depot

q: Stores having a limited shelf life are received against a purchase order, but a major part of their shelf life has already expired while the stores were with the supplier, leaving too short a residual life for their normal use. The consignment is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Accepting it in all cases at the full contract price, shelf life being the depot's concern after receipt
options.B: Accepting it and issuing it after the expiry of its shelf life
options.C: Treating the inadequate residual shelf life as a ground for rejection or for acceptance only under the orders of the competent authority, the stores being not normally acceptable with too little usable life remaining
options.D: Taking the stores into stock at a nominal value of one rupee

q: A requisition for issue of stores from a depot bears the signature of a person who is not authorised to sign requisitions on behalf of the requisitioning department. The depot correctly:

options.A: Does not issue the stores on the requisition until it is signed or authenticated by the officer authorised to requisition stores for the department
options.B: Issues the stores, the signature on a requisition being of no consequence
options.C: Issues the stores and obtains the authorised signature after the close of the financial year
options.D: Sells the stores to the person signing the requisition
